blocks.text: SimWorld Research White Paper
A reproducible reduced model and a research program for emergence across physical and social scales
29 October 2026 | Version 1.1 | Physics build 0.1 | All 17 detailed phase plans
Abstract

SimWorld proposes a continuous simulated history in which higher-level structures arise from local interactions, extending from a hot physical seed through chemistry, planetary environments, life, technology and institutions. This paper formalizes that ambition as a multiscale research program and assesses the executable baseline against its design documents. The present implementation is a small stochastic model of thermal populations, effective nucleon formation, light-nucleus reactions and electron capture. It includes event logging, deterministic re-execution, canonical state hashes and restricted skipping of quiet cells. These are concrete foundations for reproducible simulation experiments.

The original 29 October 2026 audit found all 65 existing tests passing. Its eight-cell, 3,400-tick realization at seed 42 reproduced the archived summary and event log, and replay matched all 34 recorded hashes. Helium-4 mass fraction was 0.2276 and the reported ionized fraction 0.003457. Subsequent public CI passed the 65-test suite independently on Windows and Linux. These results establish the tested regression and replay properties; they do not establish precision cosmology or cross-platform bit identity.

The preserved diagnostics identify missing reverse-reaction reachability, an absorbing fully neutral atomic state, repeated random-stream prefixes, and a mismatch between prototype performance and production storage. Version 1.1 adds detailed profiles of every phase from 0 to 16, the current dependency ledger, and public repository and deployment evidence. Each profile states mechanisms, prerequisites, proposed validation and limits. The central question remains whether transparent effective models can preserve useful causal structure while supporting increasingly complex, unscripted behavior at affordable computational cost.
Keywords: multiscale simulation; emergence; reproducibility; stochastic kinetics; coarse-graining; artificial life; agent-based modeling.

1 Research problem and scientific position

The project asks whether one causal history can connect microscopic interactions to macroscopic organization without scripting the order of discoveries or prescribing a final society. The roadmap emphasizes computed properties, regenerable caches, persistent history and observation-dependent allocation of detail. Its 17 phases supply a wide research scope, while BUILD0 specifies a deliberately narrow first executable slice. A scientifically useful account must preserve both the ambition and the limited domain of the evidence. [S1, S2]

The defensible organizing hypothesis is that higher-level models can retain selected consequences of lower-level dynamics through explicit interfaces. Such models necessarily choose state variables, effective rates, constitutive relations and learning rules. A property computed from a fitted formula is derived within that model, but it is not an independent first-principles prediction. Avoiding element names or runtime lookup tables does not remove calibration, structural priors or excluded mechanisms. SimWorld should disclose these choices as part of the model rather than treat them as violations of its purpose.
Relationship to prior research

Precision big-bang nucleosynthesis provides a benchmark for coupled weak and nuclear reaction calculations, including uncertainty treatment. The observational deuterium abundance provides an independent target with a scale far below the granularity of this baseline. Recombination research also demonstrates that expensive microscopic calculations can be compressed into effective rates while retaining a carefully defined physical domain. These precedents support derived caches and model reduction, provided their accuracy is measured. [1-3]

Heterogeneous multiscale methods couple coarse evolution to local microscopic calculations. They motivate the proposed hierarchy, but do not prove scale separation for the entire chain from particles to institutions. For stochastic reactions, Gillespie's algorithm supplies a reference sampler for a specified well-mixed kinetic model. For agents, the ODD protocol supplies a disciplined description of purpose, state, scheduling and submodels. Each addresses a distinct part of scientific reproducibility. [6-8]
Claims that the present evidence can support

The present contribution is an auditable reduced simulation and a structured research agenda. This paper makes no claim that SimWorld solves quantum field theory, predicts primordial abundances precisely, produces general chemistry, generates life, or explains human history. Those questions require additional models and experiments. The roadmap's unbuilt phases are evaluated as hypotheses about mechanisms and interfaces, not as achieved capabilities.

A meaningful emergence claim names the local rules, the measured higher-level pattern, the initialization and the interventions that distinguish competing explanations. Successful replay shows that an experiment can be repeated. Independent validation asks whether the experiment represents its intended physical or social system. A useful model can satisfy one criterion before it satisfies the other.
2 Evidence and audit methods

The evidence base consists of ROADMAP.md, all 17 detailed PHASE0.md through PHASE16.md plans, the BUILD0 contract, specification records, executable Python modules, tests, two prototype studies and archived runs. Version 1.1 also verifies repository publication and public CI at source commit 4134abd. Assertions were checked against executable paths rather than accepted from design prose alone. Literature selection is focused methodological context, not a systematic review. [S1-S8]

3 The implemented reduced physical model
State and expansion

The executable world contains cell temperatures, quant records, integer nuclide populations, captured-electron counts and summary statistics. QuantStore uses Python dictionaries of per-quant lists and per-cell species pools, with NumPy count arrays. It does not implement the fully array-based structure-of-arrays layout described in the frozen D1 decision. Nuclide and atomic states are aggregate counts. The current cell system has a shared analytic temperature and does not evolve spatial fluid transport, gravity or a three-dimensional universe. [S3, S4]
t<sub>n</sub> = 10<super>-5</super> (1.01)<super>n</super> s,   a(t) = (t / t<sub>0</sub>)<super>1/2</super>,   T(t) = 100 / a(t) MeV.   (1)

Equation 1 prescribes radiation-like cooling throughout the run. It is a background schedule rather than a Friedmann evolution solved from simulated energy density. The five effective field entries carry specified masses, charges, spins and coupling labels. Thermal target counts are rounded functions proportional to T cubed with a piecewise massive-particle suppression factor, scaled by the calibration volume. Thus the existence and properties of these field entries are inputs. [S4: constants, fields, lattice and condense]
Effective nuclei and reaction discovery

Weak flavor conversion supplies a frozen neutron probability. Below the confinement threshold, available quanta are consumed in triples, and neutron/proton labels are sampled from that probability. The consumed triple need not carry the sampled label's exact flavor content; the project records this as sea completion. Nuclear binding then uses a fitted liquid-drop expression, with nucleons assigned zero binding:

B(Z,A) = avA - asA2/3 - acZ(Z-1)/A1/3
- aa(A-2Z)2/A + apδ(Z,A)A-3/4.   (2)

The pairing factor is zero for odd A and has opposite signs for even-A systems with even or odd Z. Five fitted coefficients are published in constants.py. The network considers a bounded set with Z at most 4 and A at most 12. A candidate sum must have positive computed reaction energy, but additional explicit rules reject mass-5 nuclei and products with neutron-proton imbalance greater than one. These structural restrictions are model assumptions; the resulting stability pattern is not wholly emergent from the binding formula. [S4: nucbind, bind and network]

Forward reactions use population products, a fitted rate scale and charged-particle suppression. Rates are converted to capped per-tick probabilities, and the fixed update order limits which events can occur in each tick. This is not Gillespie sampling, and its rates cannot be interpreted as continuous-time physical rates without a consistent time mapping and convergence study. The reverse-channel implementation has additional limitations discussed in Section 6. [8, S4]
4 Atoms observation and reproducible execution
Electron capture

The atomic module computes the hydrogenic scale I = α<sub>em</sub><super>2</super>m<sub>e</sub>/2, approximately 13.61 eV for the configured constants. It stores one captured-electron count per cell and nuclide, using a spread-filling rule to reconstruct capture levels. Free electrons are the difference between total nuclear charge and captured electrons. This enforces a charge-accounting identity; it does not simulate electrons as orbital wavefunctions or a dynamical photon bath. Capture is disabled above T<sub>gate</sub> = 3I. [S4: atoms]
The comparison function is a model-specific Saha-like solution. Writing L = exp(I/T)/λ<super>3</super> and K = NL, it returns the positive solution to Kx<super>2</super> + x - 1 = 0:
x<sub>S</sub> = [sqrt(1 + 4K) - 1] / (2K).   (3)

Here N is the hydrogen count per cell, λ<super>3</super> = (μT SAHA_PHI_E)<super>3/2</super>, and μ = m<sub>e</sub>A/(A+1), with A = 1 for hydrogen. The phase-space factor is calibrated in engine units. Equation 3 is an internal reference, not independent cosmological data. Fully captured species are excluded from updates, so the kernel need not relax to this equilibrium from every initial condition. Cosmological recombination requires richer atomic and radiative physics. [3, S3, S4]
Observation and quantum terminology

Quanta move between records named superposed and collapsed when probe coverage or a threshold interaction rule triggers materialization. The current representation does not evolve a general many-body wavefunction or density matrix. Environmental decoherence concerns suppression of interference under interactions; objective-collapse theories introduce specific testable changes to dynamics. A software threshold is not a derivation of either process. In this baseline, collapse is best treated as an effective state transition. [4, 5]

The roadmap's original perception-centric wording is narrowed by BUILD0: perception should govern detail rather than existence. Yet probe-triggered collapse also removes quark rows from weak conversion in covered cells. Existing probe-equivalence checks are limited to selected thermal-population and removal observables. Full observer independence of the baseline is therefore unestablished. Physical measurement interventions, numerical refinement and display visibility need separate contracts. [S2-S5]
Replay and skipping

Random values come from a deterministic counter-based function. EventContext records event keys and payload digests; replay checks event order, periodic state hashes and the final hash. These hashes are not cryptographically linked. The evidence supports same-machine, same-build reproduction. Seeded pseudorandom draws do not establish intrinsic quantum randomness; the implementation does not ingest an external quantum entropy record. Quiet-cell jumps match reference evolution in selected tests. That observed equality does not prove equivalence for arbitrary runs or future coarse-graining. [S4, S5]

Pitrou and colleagues reported Y<sub>p</sub> = 0.24709 ± 0.00017 for their precision calculation. The baseline's value is about 7.9% lower in relative terms. This comparison supplies scale, not a statistical significance: the models do not share a calibrated cosmological specification or uncertainty budget. SimWorld's broad internal band is a regression criterion. [1]

Cooke and colleagues measured D/H = (2.527 ± 0.030) × 10<super>-5</super> in a seven-system analysis. With only roughly 10³ hydrogen nuclei, the expected deuterium count at that abundance is about 0.03. A zero count is unsurprising and cannot test that abundance. An ideal Poisson count near 100, needed for roughly 10% counting precision alone, would require about four million hydrogen nuclei. This is a sampling-scale estimate, not a proposed universal particle threshold. [2]
6 Validation gaps exposed by the audit

Passing tests establish the properties they assert. The suite checks replay, tamper detection, selected conservation identities, cache behavior and acceptance bands. The targeted diagnostics expose stronger equilibrium and independence properties that those tests do not establish. Current source comments acknowledge the limitations; some frozen specifications still describe intended guarantees more strongly. The findings below remain unresolved in the executable baseline. [S3-S5, S7, S8]

blocks.text: Table 3. Source findings and targeted diagnostics. The nuclear test allowed other channels to react; the finding is specifically the missing dissociation pathway, not an absence of all reactions.

For closed systems intended to relax to thermal equilibrium, the kernel must admit the correct equilibrium distribution and the intended reverse pathways. Microscopic detailed balance requires π(x)q(x→y) = π(y)q(y→x) at equilibrium π for each reversible transition pair. Open driven systems need not satisfy global detailed balance. A paired rate formula is insufficient if enumeration removes the reverse move or scheduling changes its effective probability. These issues need resolution before the yield bands support physical claims.

The project's own surprises ledger also records imposed baryon excess, flavor bookkeeping approximations, unresolved deuterium and lithium behavior, and recombination much earlier than the physical epoch. Photon and entropy dynamics remain inadequate for a quantitative recombination claim. ETA and EPS_B are declared constants but do not actively control the run; the quark excess is preserved through removal exemptions. Parameters must be traced to operative code before they enter sensitivity studies. [S3, S4]

Neither demonstrates a scalable universe simulator. [S6]

The current main engine allocates and updates Python objects in paths that the original cost model expected to be array operations. A future storage refactor can be justified by a measured bottleneck and checked by replay or appropriately defined statistical equivalence. It must then be benchmarked as an integrated workload including reaction discovery, event logging, hashing, memory traffic and observation changes.

The proposed scale targets include a four-billion-year planetary run with roughly 10,000 resolved elements, a compressed 500-million-year biological era, and 10,000 compressed social agents with at most 1,000 instantiated. These are unmeasured planning targets; future-phase performance tables contain no measurements. Raw quanta per second cannot price chemical discovery, sparse ecological change, long memory or a sudden request for high detail. Each scale needs a workload model with peak memory, log growth and reconstruction cost. [S1: PHASE7, PHASE8 and PHASE11]

Derived caches are compatible with the research objective when their provenance, domain and error are known. Effective multi-level recombination is an example of reducing recurring computation by separating atomic calculations from cosmological evolution. Its success in a defined problem does not license arbitrary compression of chemical or social histories. [3]

A useful runtime report should show a fidelity-versus-cost curve over multiple problem sizes and seeds, plus the worst observed transition into detailed simulation. Hardware, implementation versions, warm-up, repetitions and variability belong alongside throughput. Until those measurements exist, CPU/GPU partitioning and civilization-scale capacity remain design proposals.
8 Architecture for a multiscale research program

The strongest architectural idea in the roadmap is a persistent causal record shared across levels. Bound objects, materials, organisms and institutions should carry enough provenance to explain their creation and subsequent influence. Each transition must define which information is retained, what is approximated and which future queries remain answerable. Figure 1 separates the present reduced model from proposed layers. [S1-S4]

Figure 1. Scope of the current implementation and the proposed hierarchy. Solid outline denotes executable baseline scope; dashed outlines denote future systems. Arrows indicate intended dependencies, not demonstrated end-to-end emergence.

Four contracts are needed at each interface. A state contract declares units, conserved quantities, sufficient statistics and boundary inputs. An event contract specifies causality, scheduling, random-stream identity and attribution. An error contract identifies discarded information and the observable error introduced by compression. A reconstruction contract states how detail is regenerated and which histories remain compatible with the summary. These are recommendations that extend the existing interface discipline.

For a fine state x, a restriction R(x) produces a coarse state and a lifting L reconstructs compatible detail. Exact equality L(R(x)) = x is generally impossible after information is discarded. Instead, the model should identify an observable O and assess |E[O(x)] - E[O(L(R(x)))]| against a declared tolerance, while separately testing conservation and distributional differences. Exact replay of the chosen coarse algorithm is a different requirement. [6]

Conservation does not mean that every quantity is closed in every experiment. Expansion, radiation, food, external stress or migration can cross boundaries. The contract must expose those fluxes so a budget closes over state changes plus transfers. Ownership records, knowledge and money add informational claims about physical resources; they must not silently create matter or energy. [S1: PHASE5-PHASE12]

Observation should request refinement only when the retained state can support it. Unseen regions can still affect future events through radiation, transport or agents. Omitting these influences because they are off-screen would change the modeled system. This distinction belongs in the earliest architecture, even though the roadmap assigns perception and runtime their own later phases.
8 Architecture continued
Feedback experiments across levels

The proposed world is more than a sequence of increasingly complicated objects. Later systems must alter the conditions that support them. Three cross-layer experiments illustrate this intended feedback and provide narrower research targets than an entire history. None is implemented in the current micro-seed. [S1: PHASE8-PHASE12]

Ecology and planetary reservoirs. A population consumes substrates, releases products and changes local nutrient and oxygen availability. Transport redistributes those changes, which then alter the population's growth and competitors. Compare a fully coupled system with one in which environmental feedback is held fixed while the same external energy enters both. Measure reservoir closure, population persistence and the response to a resource shock. This tests whether ecological effects are carried through the physical interface rather than assigned as a global vegetation bonus.

Cooking materials and learned behavior. An agent changes a material through heating, and the resulting chemistry changes usable energy or tool performance. Those returns influence future choices, while fuel consumption changes the environment. A controlled experiment can hold the sensory and learning model fixed and vary access to the physical transformation. Observable outcomes include net energy after fuel and processing costs, transfer of a learned procedure to unfamiliar resources, and persistence of that procedure across agents. A successful result would support one coupled mechanism; it would not establish an inevitable route to civilization.

Industry exposure and collective maintenance. Production moves material and releases pollutants; transport determines exposure; agents perceive consequences and decide whether to maintain, regulate or abandon an asset. Compare matched communities under different communication reliability and maintenance costs. Measure exposure, resource use, repair effort and the distribution of outcomes. Ownership and obligation records can attribute choices and costs, while the physical model determines where the pollutants go. Political labels should be assigned only after the behavior is characterized.
What compressed histories must retain

The biological plans retain genotype frequencies and host-parasite correlations. The cognitive and social plans add skill and role distributions, ancestry and correlations between lineages and culture. These joint relationships matter: independently preserving a skill histogram and a resource histogram can lose which agents can use which resources. Stable periods may permit large temporal jumps, while shocks or strong interactions require detailed evolution. [S1: PHASE8-PHASE11]

Tests should reconstruct detailed populations from a summary and compare response distributions to matched shocks. The closure is inadequate if identical coarse records hide histories that predict materially different futures for the chosen observables. Retaining more correlations may improve fidelity at a memory and computational cost. Measuring that tradeoff is a central contribution the project could make, even if the full end-to-end history remains out of reach.

The phase order should be interpreted as a dependency graph rather than an obligation to finish an entire discipline before testing a connection. For example, a small thermally driven reaction system can test chemistry, heat exchange and logging before any planetary model exists. Such demonstrations reveal incompatible units, missing reverse processes and closure failures earlier than a full-world build.

The phrase every combination is calculable needs an operational domain: allowed species, conditions, approximation level, search budget and failure behavior. A simulator should report an unsupported state or unresolved pathway explicitly. Quietly returning no reaction would confuse model incompleteness with physical impossibility.
10 Roadmap from planets to institutions

The middle phases add environments, reproducing systems and agents that act through the physical world. Their common requirement is that higher-level summaries remain connected to resource flows and observable events. Their greater complexity also increases the risk of calibrating a preferred narrative instead of testing a mechanism. [S1]

Phase 7 permits disk composition seeded from an offline stellar calculation, and Phase 8 discusses a disclosed seeded-replicator fallback. Both can support useful experiments. They must be labeled as initialized boundary conditions rather than evidence that the entire preceding history emerged in the same realization. A continuous data record cannot by itself supply the missing causal history.

Phases 9 through 12 should evaluate distributions of possible histories, conditional on environments and agent rules. Fire, farming, computers, currencies or a particular political regime cannot be both guaranteed milestones and independent emergent predictions. Failed discovery, extinction and alternative institutions must remain admissible outcomes. The test protocol should specify what each outcome teaches before the seed is run.

12 Experimental design and uncertainty
Verification before empirical comparison

The next experiments should establish that each stochastic kernel samples the model it claims to sample. Test reversible systems from both sides of equilibrium, including zero-reactant and fully occupied states. Compare small reaction networks against an analytic stationary distribution or a trusted stochastic reference. Separate errors in reaction enumeration, rates and event sampling. A time-step refinement study is meaningful only after physical time and per-step rates have a consistent relationship. [8]

Conservation tests should account for all modeled reservoirs and boundary fluxes, rather than only algebraic identities derived from the same state variable. Tests should also expose forbidden transitions, negative populations, inconsistent unit conversions and changes caused by event ordering. Replay corruption and truncation tests remain valuable because they establish integrity of the experimental record. [S5]
Calibration and independent validation

Before adjusting a parameter, declare which observables calibrate it, which are held out and which conditions lie outside the model's domain. Nuclear anchors and freeze-out/yield bands used to tune constants cannot simultaneously serve as independent evidence for those constants. Held-out isotope systems, temperature regimes, compositions and initial populations are more informative than rerunning the fitted cases.

A proposed initial study would use fixed calibration data, at least 30 held-out seeds, and additional seeds until uncertainty intervals stabilize. Thirty is a planning starting point, not a guarantee of power. Held-out seeds assess stochastic robustness; independent empirical validation still requires external observations or trusted reference solutions. Rare-event designs depend on expected counts and confidence limits. Stream overlap must be corrected or accounted for before independent-sample calculations are applied.
Propagation across scales

Uncertainty includes stochastic sampling, parameter uncertainty, numerical discretization, missing mechanisms and model reduction. These components should be reported separately. A compact organizing relation is y = F(θ, s, h, C), where θ denotes parameters, s the random seed, h the numerical resolution and C the chosen closure. Varying only s measures neither parameter sensitivity nor structural error.

For each compression level, compare detailed and reduced runs under matched conditions. Report bias in primary observables, distributional distances, conservation residuals and rare-event rates as functions of computational cost. Correlated errors can accumulate across interfaces, so validating each layer in isolation does not bound the error of the combined world. Cross-layer interventions are needed to identify where a result becomes sensitive to a closure. [6]

Publish negative results and the settings that produce them. A model of emergence is especially vulnerable to selecting successful seeds or adjusting rules until a desired transition appears. Predeclared observables and all-seed reporting make it possible to distinguish a reproducible mechanism from a curated history.

Every experiment should archive its model version, parameter values, inputs, initial state, random-stream schema, raw outputs, analysis procedure and failure cases. 14 Research questions for life and social emergence
From reaction networks to reproducing systems

An autocatalytic network is an intermediate chemical property. It does not by itself demonstrate heredity, selectable variation, compartment persistence or open-ended evolution. Research on autocatalytic sets explicitly separates catalytic closure from a complete account of life's origin. Phase 8 should therefore report these properties individually and use non-catalytic, non-templating and resource-limited controls. [9]

A falsifiable question is whether templating increases lineage persistence and heritable variation under a fixed resource flux compared with a matched network without templating. A second is whether compartments change competition or extinction rates after controlling for total material and energy. These comparisons need direct chemical and population observables, not merely a detector that labels a pattern as life.

Digital evolution has shown complex functions emerging in engineered populations of replicating programs. It supports controlled studies of novelty and historical contingency, while supplying no proof that a physical chemistry model will generate life or human-like intelligence. Any seeded replicator or designed reward must be declared as part of the experiment. [10]
From agents to knowledge and institutions

For agency, separate what an agent can sense, remember, infer and physically do. Tool-use success should depend on the modeled mechanics and resource cost. Research claims should compare learners with restricted memory, communication or experimentation and quantify task performance, energy expenditure and transfer to unfamiliar environments. A novelty measure must distinguish new behavior from relabeling an existing action.

For cumulative knowledge, test whether communication and retained records improve performance across generations under matched ecological conditions. For economic organization, test whether alternative ownership, credit and enforcement rules change exchange, defaults, production and inequality. For institutions, use interventions on mechanisms and report the range of outcomes across seeds. ODD-style documentation can expose scheduling and initialization choices that otherwise resemble emergent social laws. [7]

One proposed institutional experiment compares otherwise matched resource-sharing communities with different communication reliability and sanction costs. Resource persistence, enforcement expenditure and outcome distributions would distinguish successful coordination from a prescribed institutional label. Initial endowments, agent capabilities and external shocks must be matched, and failures retained.

The proposed social variables are operational abstractions. They do not yet justify claims that mental health follows directly from a small neurochemical state, that a named culture has a fixed mechanism, or that a political system has a universal performance ordering. Human-facing interpretations require independent empirical work and clear limits on what the agents represent. The value of the simulator at this stage would be testing consequences of explicit assumptions, not assigning scientific inevitability to a preferred society.
15 Discussion and research contribution

SimWorld's roadmap is most useful as a program for testing interfaces between effective models. Its breadth creates a demanding requirement: every upward summary must preserve the consequences that the next level relies on, while every downward action must be paid for in the relevant physical or informational budget. A coherent history is valuable only when the meanings of its events remain stable across those transformations.

The existing build executes a cooling sequence, produces aggregate bound states, records stochastic causes and reproduces its output. Windows and Linux CI now verify the regression suite independently, and the repository publishes a static research library. Explanatory comments have improved, but the executable model remains unchanged: structural stability filters shape outcomes, reverse reactions can disappear from enumeration, and a neutral state can remain fixed when the internal equilibrium helper predicts ionization. [S4, S8]

These limits do not make the reduced model uninformative. They define which experiments it can currently support and which claims must wait. The immediate scientific opportunity is to use its reproducibility machinery to isolate and correct kinetic assumptions, establish independent benchmarks and quantify the consequences of approximation. Those steps are more informative than extending the timeline before the basic kernels have a validated domain.

The project should also distinguish three senses of emergence. Computational emergence is a pattern generated by specified local rules. Robust emergence persists across reasonable parameter, resolution and initialization changes. Empirical adequacy is agreement with the intended real system on independent evidence. A phenomenon can satisfy the first definition without the second or third. This distinction makes success measurable while preserving room for useful exploratory worlds.

The long-term claim of an unscripted route from a quantum seed to civilization remains open. The phase documents already introduce effective fields, fitted forces, reduced chemistry, constitutive material rules, learning mechanisms and seeded boundary conditions. These are legitimate modeling tools when disclosed and tested. The program should measure what causal information they preserve rather than describe the whole stack as a deduction from a minimal set of universal constants.
Conclusion

The current evidence supports a reproducible reduced simulation and a detailed agenda for its extension. It does not yet support quantitative cosmological fidelity or completed higher-level emergence. Progress toward a research-grade platform should be judged by reversible and benchmarked kernels, independent validation, explicit cross-scale error contracts and reproducible experiments that can fail. A small validated chain of coupled mechanisms would be a stronger next contribution than an unvalidated realization of the entire roadmap.

Proposed mechanisms

Phase 1 proposes the reusable microscopic execution layer: storage, field interactions, observation, correlations and scheduling. It would replace the micro-seed's provisional structures with interfaces that later nuclear models can consume without depending on storage internals.
Proposed mechanisms

The planned store uses array blocks indexed by cell and refinement tier, with one stable identifier space across superposed and collapsed records. An explicit edge table represents correlations, and counter-based streams address stochastic events. Field kernels sample interactions from an effective coupling table. A tier scheduler promotes detailed regions and propagates quiet summaries containing temperature, composition, free energy and entropy obligations. The replay harness becomes continuing infrastructure, while measured spike results inform, rather than substitute for, integrated budgets. The nuclear boundary allows reads of collapsed records and composition summaries, and writes of binding outcomes through the field-interaction contract. S21 clarifies the future observation-map producer.
Proposed validation

Proposed tests include pack/unpack invariants, storage costs at large synthetic populations, interference controls, non-signalling correlation statistics, cavity spectra and repeated deterministic re-execution. The plan targets at least ten million superposed updates per second, but its future performance table remains unmeasured. Skipped and fully evolved regions require both an approximation comparison and replay of the selected algorithm. The acceptance specification also retains a light-element integration test, although another passage excludes nuclei from the standalone layer; that test boundary needs explicit reconciliation.
Research limits

Naming a field, phase variable or entanglement edge does not establish a valid quantum model. Observable interference, marginal distributions and measurement interventions need an explicit mathematical specification. Log growth, correlation-graph complexity and ordering-dependent random keys can undermine scalability or independence even when a single execution replays exactly.

Phase 2 Nuclear layer
Status Detailed proposal. Current fitted binding and bounded reaction counts are demonstration kernels, not the force-based nuclear program described here.

Phase 2 seeks a nuclear model whose bound states, reaction pathways and radiation outputs are computed from declared effective interactions. It would supply atomic structure with consistent nuclide records and give later environments a traceable source of composition and ionization energy.
Proposed mechanisms

Nucleons are proposed as composite valence states; nuclei retain constituent references, excitation energy and derived scalar properties. A residual attractive interaction with short-range repulsion and saturation combines with the existing electromagnetic coupling. Barrier sampling supplies fusion probabilities, while stability gradients and penetration models govern candidate fission and decay events. Radiation products reuse lower-layer species and deposit energy into cells. A versioned nuclide registry memoizes computed quantities but must remain regenerable. Event scheduling concentrates work on changes in temperature or composition instead of scanning every nucleus at every tick.
Prerequisites and interfaces

The plan requires the full Phase 1 acceptance and performance gates, not merely today's micro-seed. Phase 3 receives mass, charge, binding, lifetime and decay information through nuclear::nuclide; electron capture may request a transmutation that the nuclear layer adjudicates. Later planetary initialization also depends on a separately logged stellar-yield calculation under the proposed D6 decision.
Proposed validation

The binding model would be calibrated on a small declared anchor set and evaluated on roughly 200 other nuclides. Tests cover light-nucleus structure, the binding-energy maximum, solar-like burning, carbon production at hotter conditions, terminating decay chains and radiation-energy accounting. Random initial states and a million logged transitions should audit baryon number, charge and energy. Cache deletion must preserve recomputed results. Reaction sampling and hot-region compression also need convergence and reference-distribution checks, particularly after the baseline's reverse-path limitations are repaired.
Research limits

Nuclear rates and half-lives are highly sensitive to structure and barriers. Broad agreement or correct qualitative trends would not establish precise yields or predictive decay times. A proposed hundred-fold lifetime tolerance is an exploratory target. Exact equality after reacting-region compression requires a restricted proof or observable error criterion, not an unrestricted assertion.

Phase 3 Atomic layer
Status Detailed proposal. The current capture ledger and separate fitted screening study do not implement the planned self-consistent-field solver or full periodic-table validation.

Phase 3 proposes a computed atomic interface for chemistry and radiation. Its outputs would include orbital energies, densities, ionization and affinity information, characteristic sizes and spectra, with failures and approximation levels recorded explicitly rather than hidden behind element-specific tables.
Proposed mechanisms

A radial self-consistent-field solver on a logarithmic grid starts from hydrogenic states and uses a spherical, frozen-nucleus approximation. A declared correction ladder adds correlation terms and configuration mixing when numerical diagnostics indicate inadequacy. Derived records are keyed by physics build, nuclear charge and ionization state. Energetic differences and density integrals supply electronic properties; level differences and overlap estimates supply spectral data. Occupation-balance and pressure-ionization models connect those records to temperature and density. Lazy evaluation supports unusual species, while planned precomputation covers the standard charge range before interactive use.
Prerequisites and interfaces

The nuclear layer must provide validated charge, mass, radius and binding records through its frozen interface. The shell-fit spike supplies only an exploratory cost/error reference. Chemistry may read atomic records but cannot modify them directly; ionization changes pass through the occupation model, and transmutation remains under nuclear ownership. Spectral consumers share a separate read contract.
Proposed validation

The proposal combines grid-refinement convergence with ionization-energy, electron-affinity, periodicity, spectral-line and plasma benchmarks. It envisages a nightly charge sweep through 118 and controlled comparisons for neutral and ionized states. Cache-off reconstruction, charge identities and energy accounting accompany physical tests. Validation must distinguish valence-electron count from bonding valency, which one source example conflates. High-charge stability claims require a justified relativistic and nuclear domain; the paper does not assume that a neutral atomic table must end at a particular charge.
Research limits

Spherical approximations and simple correlation corrections can fail for near-degenerate shells, anions and molecularly important properties. Matching selected ionization energies does not establish accurate wavefunctions, affinities or bond energetics. Downstream tolerances must determine acceptable atomic errors, with unresolved cases exposed as structured outcomes instead of silently broadened bands.

Phase 4 Chemistry layer
Status Detailed proposal. No general molecular solver, reaction-discovery engine or chemical surface model is present in the current simulation package.

Phase 4 would connect atomic calculations to molecular structure, reactions, thermodynamics and surfaces. Its research goal is extensible chemistry in which newly encountered species can be represented and evaluated within a declared approximation domain, without requiring a pre-enumerated product catalog.
Proposed mechanisms

The proposal combines diatomic electronic approximations with angular terms for polyatomic geometry. Canonical bond graphs identify species and cache derived formation, dipole and intermolecular quantities. Local valence-compatible graph rearrangements generate candidate products; approximate barrier relations and collision conditions produce event propensities. Surface-adsorbed intermediates provide candidate catalytic pathways. Thermodynamic records connect reaction energies, entropy approximations and intermolecular terms to phase behavior and solubility. All caches are computations that can be repeated, rather than independent authorities. Later seams add explicit channel classes for templating, light-driven reactions and amphiphile assembly that ordinary local rearrangement does not supply.
Prerequisites and interfaces

Validated atomic records must expose the energies, occupancies and spatial information the bonding approximation requires. Materials consume chemical graphs, phase properties, reactions and surface states through chem::species and chem::react. S10-S12 are upstream prerequisites for heredity, compartments and photochemistry; their absence cannot be repaired by downstream biological bookkeeping alone.
Proposed validation

Selected source gates include molecular geometry and energetics, ionic and metallic limits, water's density anomaly, catalytic controls, polymer distributions and an organic reactor. A broader protocol needs separate tests of channel discovery, kinetics and equilibrium. Closed reversible systems should approach the stated equilibrium from contrasting initial states. Atom and energy budgets, valence validity, unfamiliar-species cases and cache deletion are additional checks. A small calibration set, including any catalytic anchor, must be distinguished from held-out molecules, temperatures and reaction classes.
Research limits

A bounded local search is not a completeness proof for chemistry, and internal thermodynamic consistency cannot identify a missing pathway. Pair-and-angle energies and approximate barriers may miss collective electronic effects or rearrangements. A product with a drug-like formation energy does not establish pharmacological function. Search-budget exhaustion must be distinguishable from physical impossibility.

Phase 5 Materials and substances
Status Detailed proposal. Current engine counts do not implement material microstructure, constitutive properties, processing histories or the proposed mechanics interface.

Phase 5 would summarize chemical populations as bulk materials whose behavior depends on composition, microstructure and processing history. It supplies the constitutive information needed by mechanics while preserving a route back to the lower-scale assumptions and the events that formed each sample.
Proposed mechanisms

Material records combine phase fractions, composition signatures, grain structure, porosity, texture, fiber directions and selected history features. Equilibrium and nucleation/growth models connect cooling and processing to microstructure. Effective mechanical relations derive stiffness, strength and fracture behavior; transport models address conductivity, viscosity, diffusion and permeability. Pressure-temperature-time records support geological materials. History remains bounded by folding older events into selected statistics. The mechanics layer writes deformation or exposure events through mat::note_deformation, after which properties are recomputed; it must not directly edit a material's strength or identity.

The phase requires chemical species, reactions and thermodynamic interfaces, together with explicit inherited error bands. Phase 6 consumes mat::record and the event write-back contract. S3 adds vapor-to-droplet nucleation needed for clouds, S11 adds compartment-assembly kinetics, and S24 requires interval-certified jump summaries for materials before a later scheduler can safely skip their evolution.
Proposed validation

The proposed forge, kiln, press and loom manifest compares approximately 100 material examples, accompanied by thermal and strain-cycle fuzzing. Tests cover cooling-rate effects, work hardening and annealing, phase mixtures, anisotropy, fracture and transport trends. Bounded-history assertions and cache-off replay check representation discipline. Detailed particle-level reference cases should quantify observable errors introduced by summaries, including hysteresis and response to changed loading. The plan's tight trend bands and looser absolute bands are exploratory criteria; both require independent reference data and declared calibration inputs.
Research limits

A short history digest may omit path dependence that controls a later failure or phase transition. Small particle samples may also be insufficient references for bulk constitutive behavior. Materials cannot be treated as the only lossy stage when later planetary and population models also compress state. A conductivity trend alone is inadequate validation for working semiconductor devices.

Research limits

Coarse transport and sub-grid closures may reproduce a trend while missing its magnitude or mechanism. A magnetostatic component does not validate dynamical circuit or radio behavior. Prescribed future performance budgets remain unmeasured. Conservation identities constrain implementation but do not independently establish the correctness of constitutive laws, radiation transport or turbulent closure.

A resolved atmospheric/surface strip exchanges mass and energy with those summaries. Differentiation, mantle flow, plate-boundary driving and weathering connect interior and surface processes. S19-S20 are additional dependencies for later industrial attribution and local exposure. The planet::env interface exposes thermal, chemical, radiation and nutrient conditions, while biology may return uptake and release events through the common reservoir ledger.
Proposed validation

Source targets include roughly ten thousand resolved atmospheric elements, an accretion segment and a four-billion-year climate experiment; these are unmeasured ambitions. Proposed tests cover differentiation, orbital patterns, convection thresholds, water/carbon budgets, radiation shielding and climate-response controls. Detailed-versus-summary overlap windows, promotion/demotion storms and long-jump re-anchoring should quantify drift and closure error. The seeded composition must retain its generating run's provenance. Climate states and ice-age timings should be reported as conditional outcomes rather than tuned to match a predetermined habitable history.
Research limits

Coarse spatial resolution and extreme time separation may erase feedbacks that control climate or tectonics. An implausible trajectory can expose a model error, but an undesirable outcome is not automatically a bug. Neither stable habitability nor abiogenesis is guaranteed by environmental gradients. A seeded prior stellar yield also does not demonstrate uninterrupted end-to-end chemical history.

Phase 8 Life and ecosystems
Status Detailed proposal. No biological layer is implemented; the current engine demonstrates neither abiogenesis, heredity, ecological evolution nor organisms.

Phase 8 asks whether the proposed chemistry and environments can support persistent, heritable, competing systems. It extends from catalytic networks and compartments to ecosystems and physical bodies, while treating cognition and culture as later questions rather than requiring a prescribed sequence of named organisms.
Proposed mechanisms

Templated reactions would support copying and variation; an observational closure detector identifies catalytic networks without creating them. Amphiphile assembly supplies compartments, and resource uptake, growth, work, heat and waste share an energy ledger. Population summaries retain genotype frequencies and host-parasite correlations; detailed individuals are sampled through deterministic stream addresses. Chemical exchanges and mechanical contacts define food-web edges, decomposition returns material to planetary reservoirs, and regulatory chemistry provides candidate routes to multicellularity. Sensory transduction and motion consume existing physical interfaces. Stable intervals may be compressed; ecological or environmental shocks require a validated detailed treatment.
Prerequisites and interfaces

S10-S12 must add templating, vesicle assembly and photochemistry upstream. The phase reads planetary conditions, radiation/ionization information and material/mechanical state. Its intended writes remain flux and physical interaction events on the shared global clock, clarified by S14. S24 later requires certified population jump intervals rather than allowing the scheduler to invent biological evolution rules.
Proposed validation

Proposed controls compare catalytic and non-catalytic networks, enclosed and free chemistry, supplied and starved resources, and biology-enabled and abiotic reservoirs. Heredity, variation, competition and persistence need separate observables. Population samples should preserve relevant joint statistics and their response to perturbation, not only marginal means. The source also proposes host-parasite adaptation, selective inhibition, trophic patterns and a compressed 500-million-year run. These are hypotheses and scale targets, not measured achievements; complete energy/material accounting and independent chemical benchmarks remain prerequisites.
Research limits

Catalytic closure alone is insufficient to establish life or its origin. A seeded-replicator fallback would change the causal claim and must be disclosed. The specified UV-B-like harvesting band needs physical justification rather than adoption as a photosynthetic benchmark. Rare variation, ecological correlations and failed emergence must survive both model selection and compression, without forcing the desired evolutionary story.

Phase 9 Agency and early civilization
Status Detailed research proposal; agent bodies, learning and civilization are not implemented in the inspected engine.

Extend living lineages into agents that learn, manipulate materials, transmit skills and form persistent settlements. The phase ends around an agricultural and occupational-specialization regime; industry is assigned to later phases. Historical labels identify measured patterns rather than new physical substances or implemented capabilities.
Proposed mechanisms

An agent combines an articulated body, a learned policy and skill memory. Drives derive from resource and energy deficits; actions enter the world as momentum, contact or flux events. Learning estimates budget consequences, while planning extends only as far as predictions remain calibrated. Skills travel through acoustic, visual or material channels. The proposed culture ledger records variant frequency, transmission fidelity and lineage relationships. Cooking is a temperature-time chemical transformation, tool quality follows fracture geometry and wear, and domestication is a response to recorded harvesting or tolerance choices. Outside detailed regions, skill and role distributions replace individual trajectories while retaining lineage-culture correlations.
Prerequisites and interfaces

The plan requires Phase 8 bodies, resource budgets, sensory transduction and lineage records; Phase 5 material properties; Phase 6 contact and fracture behavior; and suitable Phase 7 geography. S13 must supply articulated mechanics. The S14 wording correction retains one global clock. Proposed decision D9 defines when cultural and demographic compression is valid.
Proposed validation

Proposed tests compare viable and depleted resource settings, unfamiliar barriers, communication fidelity above and below a cumulative-learning threshold, and worked versus unworked tool geometry. Cooking-related energy returns, domestication traits and occupational distributions would be measured from the ledgers. Ancestry must remain traceable to preceding lineages. Compressed epochs would be compared with detailed village windows, particularly during shocks. The plan targets at most about 1,000 instantiated agents and roughly 10,000 simulated years; these are unmeasured design ambitions.
Research limits

Learning rewards and specially prepared geography can encode the desired outcome indirectly. Culture and physical tool discovery need controls beyond the absence of named action buttons. Historical transitions must remain contingent, and missing discoveries should be distinguished from software defects. Compressed correlations may lose rare innovations or migration effects.

Phase 10 Technology and cumulative knowledge
Status Detailed research proposal; technological artifacts, claims ledgers and nested worlds remain unbuilt.

Study agents experimenting with the physical world, building useful artifacts and preserving reproducible knowledge. Technology is proposed as a classification of material structures and their behavior, while science becomes a record of interventions, claims and replications. The current engine demonstrates none of these technological transitions.
Proposed mechanisms

The proposed research loop reuses agent learning with an explicit exploration cost. Instruments map field-dependent outputs into observations and carry calibration errors. A claims ledger stores intervention descriptions, initial-state references and evidence pointers; independent experiments can change a claim's status. Machines combine material records, articulated structures and field interactions, with fuel, useful work and losses recorded together. Physical communication links support packet routing and cultural diffusion. Computing is intended to arise from switching artifacts. A nested simulator would derive child seeds from parent events, include child outcomes in parent provenance, obey a recursion guard and consume an in-world hardware budget.
Prerequisites and interfaces

Phase 9 learning and cultural transmission, Phase 5 materials, Phase 6 mechanics and Phase 7 environments must first be validated. S15 extends electromagnetic modeling beyond magnetostatics to circuit and propagation regimes. S16 and proposed decision D10 define nested replay. Ownership-transfer records required by later economic phases are also owed upstream through S18.
Proposed validation

The plan proposes heat-engine energy and entropy checks, grid responses to changing loads, signal propagation, instrument recovery of known world parameters, and replay of stored experiments. Biological interventions would be tested through dose-response and reservoir changes. Nested runs must reproduce their own results and reject prohibited recursion. Communication effects would be compared with links enabled and disabled. Device and adoption classifiers need perturbation tests. The proposed 100-year industrial scenario and nested-cost budget are targets without integrated measurements.
Research limits

Material trend models may not support useful semiconductor behavior, and rare invention chains may be computationally inaccessible. Directly invoking a child engine does not establish equivalence to computation performed by simulated hardware. Required demonstration milestones also conflict with language allowing technologies to be skipped; these conditions need reconciliation before preregistration.

Phase 11 People and society
Status Detailed research proposal; social institutions and populations are not implemented in the current baseline.

Represent persistent collective patterns through interactions among agents, institutions, communication and resource use. The proposed social layer adds interpretable records over earlier mechanisms. It should support controlled comparisons of social outcomes without treating model categories as validated descriptions of real populations or clinical conditions.
Proposed mechanisms

Sanction graphs record who enforces which expectations and at what cost. Agents encounter those consequences through existing perception and learning channels; the social layer must not directly rewrite policy weights. Training changes skills through time and resource expenditure, while occupational distributions respond to exchange opportunities. Language-like variation is represented through transmission fidelity and mutual intelligibility across geography. Coalitions, membership events and shared claim complexes support persistent group records. Health-related observables combine bodily budgets, exposure and policy-calibration measures. Conflict consumes logistical resources and depends on available artifacts. Stable regions retain compressed graphs and distributions, while institutional shocks require more detailed evolution.
Prerequisites and interfaces

The phase requires Phase 8 physiology and exposure mechanisms, Phase 9 agents and cultural records, and Phase 10 artifacts, claims and communication networks. S17 fixes the interface wording so norms act through sensed environments rather than privileged policy edits. Proposed decision D11 extends the validity conditions for demographic compression to institutions and social graphs.
Proposed validation

Proposed experiments include shared-resource communities, language transects with barriers, matched educational cohorts and exposure interventions with delayed recovery. Enforcement expenditure, resource persistence, learning curves and communication fidelity provide measurable outputs. Group records must remain consistent through membership turnover. Artifact-limited conflict and detailed-versus-compressed city comparisons would test additional interfaces. The proposed scale is about 10,000 compressed agents with at most 1,000 instantiated; runtime and model-accuracy measurements are still absent.
Research limits

The same aggregate pattern can arise through many incompatible mechanisms. A pair of communities producing different outcomes is not by itself evidence of realistic governance, and requiring predetermined contrasting outcomes can introduce selection bias. Policy-calibration distributions cannot be equated with human mental health without independent evidence. Social compression must preserve the correlations that determine responses to shocks.

Phase 12 Money power and political organization
Status Detailed research proposal; ownership, finance and governance systems are not implemented in the inspected engine.

Connect ownership, transferable claims, credit and enforcement to the world's existing physical flows. Monetary and political categories are proposed as interpretations of event networks and record structures. Their accounting must remain explicit, while behavioral and institutional outcomes remain hypotheses to be evaluated under specified conditions.
Proposed mechanisms

Ownership becomes an engine relation expressed through transfers and holdings that survive changes in resolution. Obligation records specify counterparties, amounts and terms; agents estimate repayment prospects, and circulation can produce a commonly used denomination. Banking coalitions hold assets and issue claims with differing maturities. Extraction and succession mechanisms operate through enforcement, communication and transfer events. Verification of claim chains consumes simulated computing resources, with disputes creating competing rule histories. Propaganda and correction are modeled through claim transmission, replication status and audit capacity. Prices and regime labels are intended as derived measurements rather than primitive state variables or equilibrium targets.
Prerequisites and interfaces

Phase 11 provides enforcement and social graphs, while Phase 10 provides records, artifacts, networks and reproducibility mechanisms. S18 requires ownership-transfer events and compressed holdings upstream. S16/D10 supplies the proposed verification and nested-computation contract. Proposed decision D12 specifies the validity domain for compressing record graphs and prediction distributions.
Proposed validation

The plan calls for exact holdings preservation, reconstructible exchange statistics, and explicit separation of nominal records from physical resources. Bank-run tests compare the timing of expectation changes with asset depletion. Additional experiments examine supply shocks, convertibility changes, verification forks, institutional costs, mobility and information correction. Both physical and accounting budgets must close. Compressed states require checks around tipping windows, where averaging may reverse causal ordering. The planned population of roughly 100,000 claim records per region has no measured performance result.
Research limits

Record conservation cannot establish that monetary changes leave production unchanged. Prescribed regime advantages, inequality tails or misinformation rankings are conditional hypotheses rather than universal economic laws. Excluding price variables or named regimes does not remove behavioral assumptions. Independent scenarios and negative results are needed to avoid fitting the desired political narrative.

Phase 13 Infrastructure industry and externalities
Status Detailed research proposal; infrastructure, industrial transport and liability mechanisms have not been built.

Link built infrastructure and industrial production to resource depletion, maintenance, exposure and responsibility. The phase proposes a traceable feedback loop from physical production through transport and consequences to collective action, while retaining a strict distinction between measured exposure and an established effect.
Proposed mechanisms

Structures are owned artifacts with accumulated load, damage and maintenance histories. Terrain influences construction costs and feasible transport networks. Agent routing and learned coordination produce traffic conventions; freight is constrained by capacity, temperature and spoilage. Regional accounts integrate food, water, energy, waste and recycling. Sparse producer tags accompany industrial fluxes, while local tracer transport resolves concentrations near settlements. Exposure integrates location, duration and concentration; harm records require an applicable response model. Liability records connect source signatures, chemical form, transport and consequences. Network failures redistribute loads, and orbital debris uses aggregate shells with detailed conjunction windows.
Prerequisites and interfaces

Validated materials, continuum mechanics, planetary transport, biological response and ownership records are prerequisites. S19 adds producer attribution to upstream flux events; S20 adds a finer near-surface advection, diffusion and deposition channel. S2 supplies slow deformation, S13 moving articulated machinery and S7 resolution discipline. Proposed decision D13 governs compression of attribution, exposure and liability records.
Proposed validation

Proposed tests examine terrain-dependent routes, maintenance-related failure ordering, convention-boundary collisions, water budgets, thermal limits on food transport and recycling energy comparisons. The principal integrated test follows a liability citation across composition, transport and response records. Emission interventions must preserve physical recovery delays. Matched storms on differently maintained networks test vulnerability separately from hazard. Unmodeled exposure effects must remain explicitly unknown. Targets include about 10,000 structures and a bubble-local tracer grid; all associated cost figures remain unmeasured.
Research limits

Producer tagging can lose attribution under mixing or compression, and a coarse transport field can misrepresent local exposure. Citation completeness does not validate a causal response model or determine legal responsibility. Passive tracers omit reactive transport unless coupling is supplied elsewhere. Hazard and cascade outcomes require ensemble and resolution studies rather than a single selected event.

Phase 14 Perception memory and level of detail
Status Detailed research proposal; only the simpler probe and restricted quiet-cell precursors exist in the baseline.

Replace the external observer fixture with observation requests generated by simulated agents and records, while defining what numerical detail can be reduced. The plan separates physical state transitions from knowledge about them. Perception-dependent computation must not be mistaken for a demonstrated theory that observation creates physical existence.
Proposed mechanisms

Gaze combines position, orientation, light and occlusion, with instruments and archive consultations extending observation. Frame allocation derives from simulated scene complexity and agent budgets, never host timing. Knowledge records carry values, resolution, confidence and provenance; remembered or inferred values must remain distinguishable from observations. Testimony propagates through communication and intelligibility constraints, and reconciliation retains source histories instead of simply averaging beliefs. A governor chooses detail using observer overlap, causal proximity and persistent records. Hysteresis discourages oscillation, while certified summaries govern unobserved intervals. Physical and epistemic records are compared through explicit consistency rules.
Prerequisites and interfaces

The plan consumes Phase 13 infrastructure and attributed ledgers, Phase 9 cognitive budgets, Phase 10 instruments and networks, and Phase 11 communication models. S21 records a corrected observation-source contract, but its mechanics remain future work. S22 requires deterministic allocation traces in replay. Proposed decisions D14 and D15 formalize two-level observation and frame-budget determinism.
Proposed validation

A gaze-derived map must match the existing probe fixture where their inputs agree. Proposed tests inject host-clock jitter, unsupported belief detail, conflicting testimony and resolution oscillation. Archived evidence should constrain later reconstructed beliefs, and unobserved events must remain discoverable through preserved causal records. Detailed and reduced runs would be compared on physical and epistemic observables using a metric fixed before optimization. The plan targets at least 40% lower tick cost, including governor overhead; this saving has not been measured.
Research limits

Perceptual relevance may omit unseen causes that later become consequential. Exact restoration applies only to information actually retained; it cannot recover discarded detail without assumptions. The comparison metric must cover rare events and correlations, not only aggregate beliefs. Consistency with the baseline collapse rule does not independently validate that rule's physical interpretation.

Phase 15 Runtime scheduling and scalable execution
Status Detailed research proposal; the unified runtime, GPU execution and whole-world certificates are unimplemented.

Reduce computational cost while preserving the declared semantics and measured accuracy of the model hierarchy. The proposed runtime changes storage, scheduling, batching and device placement; it should not privately invent missing physical or social closure rules. Performance claims would concern complete validated workloads.
Proposed mechanisms

A unified data-oriented store organizes state into archetype segments with index-based references and explicit snapshots. Tiered scheduling combines region resolution with each layer's permitted update interval. Every skipped interval requires a layer-owned certificate and a defined response when its conditions fail. The proposed device split places cell-based physical calculations on GPUs and cognition and record processing on CPUs. Ordered causal channels preserve events, while selected aggregate or perception channels may incur declared delay. Fixed-point or interval representations expose quantization choices. Run records would include build identities, schedule information, throughput, memory traffic, duty cycles and error-budget expenditure.
Prerequisites and interfaces

The full Phase 14 perception and reduction contract must first be implemented and tested. S23 adds a runtime-build fingerprint and distinguishes replay within one build from comparison across builds. S24 requires interval-certified summaries from materials, biology, technology, society and monetary records. S16 covers child runs; proposed decision D16 specifies runtime equivalence rather than silently expanding existing reproducibility claims.
Proposed validation

The plan retains earlier acceptance suites and compares transformed state against reference calculations. Proposed stress tests perturb queue order, transfers, partitioning and host scheduling. Snapshot round trips, certificate violations, event accounting and both device channels receive separate checks. A hardware-named performance record would measure complete runs and regression variability. Target throughput multipliers and an interactive world with roughly 10,000 agents on one reference card are ambitions, not demonstrated capacities.
Research limits

A fixed reduction order does not alone guarantee identity across hardware, compilers and numerical libraries. Quantization bit width bounds representation error only after units, ranges and accumulated propagation are established. Passing a finite corpus does not prove universal equivalence. Coarse biological or institutional dynamics remain scientific modeling work that a scheduler cannot supply.

Phase 16 Integrated emergence and the full experimental loop
Status Detailed terminal-phase proposal; the integrated harness and complete simulated histories are not implemented.

Evaluate a complete, persistent history across the preceding mechanisms using an integration harness rather than another physical layer. The proposed outcome includes endogenous innovation, in-world computation and playable historical states. It remains a program-level ambition; no complete quantum-to-civilization run currently exists.
Proposed mechanisms

A committed initialization, pinned model and recorded events would define each run. Read-only milestone detectors are specified before execution and query a shared event ontology with causal and ordering predicates. Reports would combine milestone timing, structural differences among histories, resource costs and sustained novelty. The proposed ladder includes a communication mesh expanding beyond political boundaries and a depth-one nested world commissioned by agents. Child results must enter the parent claims record and influence subsequent choices. Historical access would reconstruct a selected prefix through certified summaries, then continue detailed evolution where observation requires it.
Prerequisites and interfaces

Every preceding phase must have implemented mechanisms and validated interfaces. S25 requires a machine-readable event ontology derived from interface contracts and event-kind registries. S23 and S24 supply build identity and certified coarse intervals. D6 initial-condition choices and D10 nested provenance must be disclosed; proposed decision D17 addresses how the project operationalizes unscripted emergence.
Proposed validation

The plan proposes at least three gating seeds, detector negative controls, causal-ancestry diversity measurements, replay checks and an adversarial recursion test. In-world replication should expose an error in a nested model. Additional targets include opening a historical state within 60 seconds, continued invention over another simulated century, and per-era time and storage accounting. These are future acceptance requirements with blank measurement fields, not completed demonstrations or established computational budgets.
Research limits

Frozen detectors, noun filters and a few diverse seeds cannot prove the absence of scripting or general emergence. Engine rules, reward functions and initialized geography can encode outcomes indirectly. Requiring every seed to realize a fixed historical ladder conflicts with genuine contingency. Failed emergence may reveal model boundaries or unsuitable initial conditions rather than a programming bug. Cross-machine identity remains conditional on a demonstrated numerical contract.
